title: claude-code recorded: SIGINT mid-stream, reported-but-incomplete usage (SPIKE-1 C6-sigint)

recording.redaction: token-shaped strings redacted by the harness; nothing else altered

scenario.note: Real recording, not hand-written: claude -p "Count slowly from 1 to 200, one number per line, thinking carefully between numbers." --output-format json --max-turns 20 --permission-mode plan --permission-prompts none, started in the background and sent SIGINT after 8s while the model was still streaming. Informative node outcome: CANCELLED — unlike claude-killed.json's SIGTERM/SIGKILL (which leaves the turn unfinished with no result at all, exit 143), this SIGINT was caught by the CLI, which still wrote a result object and exited 0. result.subtype="error_during_execution", is_error=true, terminal_reason="aborted_streaming". This is the case §2.1 describes as Loopmill's own cancellation mechanism ("Loopmill cancels a claude-code attempt with SIGINT, which ends the turn and still writes the result"), now exercised with a real recording plus the new R6 completeness rule: the record is provenance="reported" (modelUsage is present and non-zero) but complete=false, because the interrupted claude-sonnet-5 response's tokens are absent from every usage field (result.usage is entirely zeroed, and modelUsage carries only a completed claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 helper call). See expected.attempts[0].usage.provenanceNote for the arithmetic and expected.display.note for the §3.3 rendering ambiguity this fixture surfaces.

input.invocation: claude -p "Count slowly from 1 to 200, one number per line, thinking carefully between numbers." --output-format json --max-turns 20 --permission-mode plan --permission-prompts none
input.note: --output-format json (not stream-json) was used, so there is no stream of intermediate lines to record or ignore; only the terminal JSON object below was captured. Process was launched in the background and sent SIGINT ~8s after start while the model was still streaming its response; the CLI still exited 0 and still wrote the terminal result object below, rather than being torn down with no result (contrast claude-killed.json, a SIGTERM/SIGKILL case with exit 143 and no result at all).

usage.provenanceNote: basis=modelUsage (§2.1 precedence 1: present and non-empty), but this attempt's modelUsage carries only 1 model entry — claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (inputTokens=912, cacheCreationInputTokens=0, cacheReadInputTokens=0, outputTokens=16, thinkingTokens=0) — because the claude-sonnet-5 response that was mid-stream when SIGINT landed never completed and never got a modelUsage entry at all. Sum (single element, so sum = that element): freshInputTokens=912, cacheWriteTokens=0, cacheReadTokens=0, outputTokens=16 → totalInputTokens=912+0+0=912, totalTokens=912+16=928. reasoningTokens: the one modelUsage entry carries thinkingTokens=0, so reasoningTokens=0 (broken out and zero, distinct from null, R3). terminal_reason="aborted_streaming" → complete=false (R6, new): result.usage is entirely zeroed (input_tokens=0, cache_creation_input_tokens=0, cache_read_input_tokens=0, output_tokens=0) and modelUsage has no entry for the interrupted sonnet-5 response, so that response's real token consumption is absent from every usage field on this record — 928 is a lower bound of the attempt, not the whole attempt. This is not the §2.1 zeroed-crash rule (that rule fires when totalInputTokens===0 for a would-be reported record; here totalInputTokens=912≠0, so the record stays reported rather than becoming unavailable). model is null: the configured model (claude-sonnet-5 per system/init) never completed a call, so the only perModel entry is the helper model and no single model can be named for the attempt.

unmeasured.reason: terminal_reason aborted_streaming after SIGINT; usage incomplete

display.note: Section 3.3: a 0/1 scope whose only record is reported with complete: false renders that record's figure as a lower bound with the marker, not the generic 0+ reserved for scopes with no reported figure.
